problemStatement.formal: For every sufficiently small positive epsilon and every 0 < C < Cprime, produce natural numbers a, b, n with epsilon*n < a and epsilon*n < b, with a! * b! dividing n! * (a + b - n)!, and with C * log n < a + b - n < Cprime * log n.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the factorial-divisibility construction behind Erdos problem 728: there are infinitely many large triples, and in the final form the overlap a+b-n can be forced into an arbitrarily prescribed logarithmic window.
whyMatters: The result is a nontrivial asymptotic divisibility construction involving factorial valuations.
It combines p-adic valuation accounting, carry estimates, and analytic bounds into a large verified Lean proof.
The entry is marked as an AI milestone because the proof is fully formalized without sorries or axioms.

proven: Definitions for the factorial valuation quantities W, kappa, N_pj, J_p, V_p, X_p, and the good_triples predicate are formalized.
Large-prime and small-prime carry/spike estimates are proved through lemmas such as lemma_forced_carries_largep, lemma_N_pj_le_ceil, lemma_bad_carries_bound, and lemma_sum_bad_spikes_le_bound.
The good triples form an infinite set for every positive C and sufficiently small positive epsilon (Lean: erdos_728).
The final factorial-divisibility statement produces a, b, n with logarithmic bounds C log n < a + b - n < Cprime log n (Lean: erdos_728_fc).
knownResults.goal: Document the verified factorial-divisibility theorem and its supporting p-adic valuation construction.
